Find hits with CAMERA

Source: R/camera_method.R
find_camera_hit.Rd

Finds the genes whose barcodes are depleted (or enriched) in the comparison given by the contrast, using the CAMERA method of Wu and Smyth (2012), camera. CAMERA is a gene set test: here each gene is a set of barcodes, and the barcodes of the gene are compared with all the other barcodes (a competitive test). Unlike find_roast_hit, it also works with a single control sample (for example a plasmid library).

Usage

find_camera_hit(
  screenR_Object,
  matrix_model,
  contrast,
  number_barcode = 3,
  thresh = 1e-04,
  lfc = 1,
  direction = c("Down", "Up"),
  fdr = 0.05,
  fdr_method = c("BH", "storey"),
  keep_all = FALSE
)

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object, normalized with normalize_data. The model uses its raw counts with its effective library sizes as offsets, the same normalization as the plots and the data table (see create_edger_obj).

matrix_model

The design matrix of the linear model, for example created with create_design_matrix (or with model.matrix). Rows must be named with sample identifiers in object order (see create_design_matrix); mismatched names or order are errors. Named contrast coefficients are aligned to design columns.

contrast

The comparison to test: the name or index of a column of matrix_model, a numeric contrast vector (for example created with create_contrast) or a one-column matrix created with makeContrasts.

number_barcode

Only genes with more than number_barcode barcodes are tested (default 3, so a gene needs at least 4 barcodes). The barcodes of a gene are tested together as a set, so this is not a number of barcodes that must change.

thresh

Deprecated and ignored: it never had an effect on the result. Filter the returned table on the FDR column instead.

lfc

Deprecated and ignored: it never had an effect on the result.

direction

The direction of the change: "Down" (default) for depleted genes or "Up" for enriched genes.

fdr

The FDR threshold: only genes with an FDR lower than or equal to this value are returned (default 0.05). Use fdr = 1 to return all the genes with the given direction.

fdr_method

How the FDR is computed: "BH" (Benjamini-Hochberg, the default) or "storey" (Benjamini-Hochberg multiplied by the estimated proportion of genes without effect, less conservative when many genes have an effect).

keep_all

Keep genes with either observed direction (default FALSE). Their PValue still tests the requested direction. Use keep_all = TRUE and fdr = 1 to obtain complete tables for combine_consistent_hits. Direction records the observed direction; it does not change the direction of the one-sided test.

Value

A tibble with one row for each hit (restricted to the observed requested direction unless keep_all = TRUE) and the columns Gene, NGenes (the number of barcodes of the gene), Direction, PValue (the one-sided p-value for the requested direction), FDR and Log2FC (the median log2 fold change of the barcodes of the gene).

Details

The raw counts are modelled with edgeR (the dispersion is estimated with estimateDisp), and camera tests the barcodes of each gene together, accounting for the correlation between them. The two-sided p-values of camera are converted into one-sided p-values for the requested direction and the FDR is computed from them over all the tested genes.

CAMERA is a competitive test: it compares the barcodes of each gene with all the other barcodes, so when many genes have an effect it becomes conservative. find_roast_hit with method = "fry" (self-contained) does not have this limitation, and neither does find_gene_zscore_hit with control genes as reference, as long as the control genes behave like genes without effect (see its documentation).

See also

find_roast_hit, find_gene_zscore_hit, find_time_hit, summarise_hits, plot_barcode_hit, create_design_matrix, create_contrast

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))

matrix <- create_design_matrix(object)
contrast <- create_contrast(matrix, treatment = "Treated",
    control = "Control")

result <- find_camera_hit(
    screenR_Object = object,
    matrix_model = matrix, contrast = contrast
)
#> Warning: 3rows with all zero counts
#> Warning: Zero sample variances detected, have been offset away from zero
head(result)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   Gene     NGenes Direction    PValue     FDR Log2FC
#>   <chr>     <dbl> <fct>         <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 Gene_173     10 Down      0.0000160 0.00856 -0.429
